subject: Infra separation & SLOs — next steps and clarification
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@hmr-analytics.com>, procurement@hmr-analytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Infra separation & SLOs — next steps and clarification

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what you told us on the call:
- Primary concern: unpredictable latency during batch/ingest spikes — worried about "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared hosted tiers.
- SLO targets: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms, p99 ideally <= 600ms for your interactive UI flows.
- Minimum throughput: ~150 qps sustained during trading hours with peaks to ~400 qps for 30-45s bursts.
- Data residency/segmentation: all customer data must remain in your VPC; audit logs needed for SOC 2.

Qualification notes: based on the above, Dedicated capacity or Private (VPC) deployment is likely the best fit. Hosted API (shared) risks adding variability unless we apply strict resource reservations and isolation policies.

Proposed next steps (we agreed):
1) I’ll share a short SLO & isolation checklist + Dedicated factsheet for your infra/security team (attached).
2) Set up a 60-min technical deep-dive with our Infra SE to map your peak patterns to capacity profiles — suggested window: Mon/Tue next week.
3) Procurement: if you want rough pricing for Dedicated, we’ll provide an MRC estimate and a PO template for finance.

Attachments: Redwood-dedicated-factsheet.pdf, SLO-and-isolation-checklist.xlsx, PO-template.docx (stubs attached).

Liam — can you confirm: do you want the deep-dive to focus on a Dedicated pool in our managed infra, or do you prefer Private (VPC) from the start? Confirming this will help us pick the right SE and prep materials.

I’ll also loop Monica (our solutions lead) and Stephanie (enterprise ops) to help with the SLO mapping and procurement flow.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra separation & SLOs — next steps and clarification

Thanks for the recap, Aditya. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side after discussing with infra: 

1) Isolation: our security team dislikes any multi-tenant "noisy neighbor" risk. They'd like strict isolation for peak windows (10:00–12:00 ET), meaning dedicated GPU pools or bare-metal placement. Temporary burst to other tenants is a deal-breaker unless it’s behind our control.

2) SLOs: the p95/p99 numbers you listed are what we'd expect. We also need a documented escalation path and an SLA credit model if p99 breaches last > 5 minutes. Can Redwood commit to measurable SLO reporting and an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if you need to mitigate capacity issues?

3) Data: VPC peering plus customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK) are mandatory.

We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity first; Private VPC/on-prem might be considered later if the Dedicated deployment can't guarantee isolation and SLO enforcement.

Next steps from our side: procurement asked for an initial commercial estimate and the PO template (please send). Also, please propose 2 slots for the technical deep-dive; prefer Tue/Wed morning ET.

Regards,
Liam Chen
Head of Platform | HM-R Analytics
liam.chen@hmr-analytics.com

Subject: Re: Infra separation & SLOs — next steps and clarification

Appreciate the clarity, Liam — this aligns with what we need to cover. Quick answers and concrete next steps: 

Isolation and deployment options:
- Dedicated capacity (recommended first step): Dedicated GPU pools reserved to your org. We provide per-pool isolation guarantees (no compute-sharing across customers) and can place workloads on dedicated instances during your peak windows. This is the lowest-friction path to remove noisy-neighbor risk without a full Private deployment.
- Private (VPC) deployment: full network isolation and customer-managed control plane; best for strict compliance/BYOK requirements but adds lead time.
- Hosted shared tier: we can offer workload reservations and priority routing, but it does not meet your "no temporary cross-tenant bursting under customer control" requirement. So not recommended for peak-sensitive UI flows.

SLOs and reporting:
- We can commit to per-route p95/p99 reporting and night/day breakdowns in Redwood Console. For contractual SLA credits, we provide clear credit terms for sustained p99 violations (>5 minutes) — terms to be negotiated in the contract.
- Automatic fallback: we support configurable fallback policies (route to fallback model or degrade to a lower-concurrency pathway) — we will include this in the deep-dive.

Security & data controls:
- VPC peering + BYOK supported for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs and retention windows can be set to meet SOC 2 requirements.

Attachments: I’m attaching the PO template and the SLO checklist back for your procurement & infra teams.

Suggested deep-dive slots (60m):
- Tue, 19 May 2026 10:30–11:30 ET (7:30–8:30 PT)
- Wed, 20 May 2026 09:00–10:00 ET (6:00–7:00 PT)

Monica/Stephanie — can you confirm which slot works and which SE (infra or security) should join?

Liam — if Dedicated is the route, we’ll also send a short capacity sizing worksheet to fill out so our capacity team can pre-size a proposal.

Thanks,
Aditya
